label: Fused MoE output
mechanism: the routed-expert output epilogue — routing-weight multiply, un-permute and top-6 slot reduction — becomes ONE Triton kernel that reads each pair row once, instead of six eager passes over the P x 6144 pair-row space
hypothesis: kernels/moe_gemm_w4a4.py step 4 is the last eager chain in the routed-expert path and the biggest one left in the engine. It exists only because CUTLASS's grouped-GEMM epilogue is fixed (per-expert alpha), so the routing weight has to be applied afterwards — the W4A16 twin (kernels/moe_gemm.py) applies its weight inside its own GEMM and never had this chain. To apply ONE scalar per row and add top_k=6 rows together it makes six passes over the P x K pair-row space (P = T*6, K = 6144): a gather, an fp32 upcast, the multiply, the bf16 round, an un-permute scatter of the full bf16 P x K tensor, and the slot reduction — ~4.3 GB of HBM per MoE layer at a canonical 6-row cohort (T = 4800, P = 28,800), of which only 0.41 GB (gather in, T x K out) is irreducible. The fused form deletes the intermediates outright: with rows[p] = dst[perm_inv[p]] (one P-element int32 scatter replacing the P x K bf16 one) the whole epilogue is the token-major read out[t] = sum_s bf16(c2[rows[t*6+s]] * topk_weights[t,s]), one program per (token, K block), the weight applied in registers between the load the reduction already had to do and the store it already had to make. The `wt` gather disappears too — the kernel reads topk_weights in its original layout. This lives in BOTH phases (exp-0015b routed decode through the same function), so the arms cover both, and the decode step is CUDA-graph captured, which the kernel is built for: fixed grid from the static padded batch, no device->host sync, no allocation, no atomics, no autotune. ONE VARIABLE: kernels/moe_out.py (new, 1 kernel + 1 wrapper) plus the one call site that reads it, behind PYENGINE_FUSED_MOE_OUT=0, which restores the eager chain verbatim. Nothing else in the traversal moves.
predicted_delta: +8 to +15% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 556-592 vs the accepted exp-0026 row 514.2 (merge bar 515.7). Cycle model from that row's own block (609 s, 2381 requests, 304,768 tokens): every request is prefilled and exp-0017 admits cohorts of 6, so the box holds ~2381/6 = ~397 grouped prefill traversals, each paying this epilogue 63 times (the W4A4 MoE layers; layer 2 is the bf16-grouped twin and layers 0-1 are dense). At the measured in-situ MIXED-step saving that is 397 x 0.162 = 64.3 s of the 609 s box; the decode side adds 304,768/64 = ~4,760 steps x 2.8 ms = ~13 s. CALIBRATION on the two rows this replaces, both measured on these same two arms: exp-0025 measured -163 ms mixed (model 64.7 s) and delivered +12.4%, which back-solves to 67.1 s actually removed = 1.04x its model; exp-0026 measured -69 ms mixed (model 27.4 s) and delivered +2.8% = 16.7 s = 0.61x its model. Applying that realized/model range [0.61, 1.04] to both terms gives S in [47, 81] s, i.e. 609/(609-S) = +8.4% to +15.3%. The isolated arm sizes the ceiling honestly: 2.145 -> 0.075 ms per layer is 2.07 ms x 63 layers = 130 ms of pure kernel time per traversal, and the in-situ prefill step moved -259 ms, so the in-situ figure is NOT the isolated arm extrapolated — it also collects the allocator and launch cost of the five deleted intermediates.

Stated plainly: this is the SAME agree_rate as the accepted exp-0026 tree (0.9625, same 15 disagreeing positions) with delta_mean moved by +0.000117 — the epilogue change is very nearly invisible to the gate, which is what the isolated arm predicts. local_pregate.isolated: tests/t_fused_moe_out (log /workspace/logs/t_fused_moe_out_exp0027_out.log), on a real routing draw at both phases' shapes. arm a DRIFT: graphed decode shape (T=64, P=384) bitwise equal, 0 of 393,216 elements; prefill cohort shape (T=4800, P=28,800) differs in 6 of 29,491,200 elements (2.0e-7), max|d| 3.125e-2 = ONE bf16 ulp at that magnitude. Both forms accumulate all six slots in fp32 and round once — the only thing that moved is the order torch's .sum(dim=1) schedules that six-term reduction, the B3.1/B3.3 class exp-0013/0023/0025/0026 introduced and D13 covers. This is not a precision reduction. arm b: two identical fused calls bitwise equal at both shapes. arm c SPEED on the prefill shape: eager 2.145 ms/layer moving ~4.31 GB (2.01 TB/s), fused 0.075 ms/layer moving ~0.41 GB (5.48 TB/s) = 28.6x.
local_pregate.insitu: tests/t_fused_moe_out_insitu (log /workspace/logs/t_fused_moe_out_insitu_exp0027_out.log), real resident model through the real Scheduler, layer split [16,17,16,17], arms INTERLEAVED off/on/off/on after a discarded warm-up of both. Each run drops engine._graphrun first so the captured decode step is captured under the arm being timed — without that the graph would keep the first arm's kernels forever and the decode term would be invisible. PREFILL step 0 (8 rows): 0.808 -> 0.550 s = 1.471x (-259 ms). MIXED step 1 (6 prefill + 8 decode): 1.124 -> 0.962 s = 1.169x (-162 ms). DECODE-only steps: 71.9 -> 69.1 ms mean over 6+6 steps (-2.8 ms), the both-phases term. SCHEDULE total 2.148 -> 1.718 s = 1.250x. The fused arm is also the steadier one (step 0: 0.548/0.551 across runs vs the eager arm's 0.738/0.879).
local_pregate.determinism: arm b of t_fused_moe_out (two identical kernel calls bitwise equal at both shapes) and arm c of t_fused_moe_out_insitu (two identical fused SCHEDULES produce bitwise-identical token streams; the eager arm does too). The kernel has a fixed grid (token x K block), no atomics, no autotune, no shape-dependent scheduling, and each output element is written by exactly one program from a fixed-order register accumulation. The only new host-side op, rows[perm] = dst, is an exact-integer scatter of a permutation — no sync, capture-legal.
local_pregate.arm_b_tokens: REPORTED, not asserted: the same schedule under the two arms diverges in 1 of 14 sequences (56 tokens). That is the expected consequence of the one-ulp reduction-order drift amplified through 66 layers, the same class every accepted fused kernel in this lineage produced; the binding gates are the TF envelope (green above) and same-schedule determinism (green).

kill_switch: PYENGINE_FUSED_MOE_OUT=0 restores the eager gather/upcast/scale/round/scatter/reduce chain verbatim
risks: (a) The decode-side term only exists if the CUDA graph is captured with the flag in the state the run uses; the flag is read once at import in the serving process (the exp-0013 convention), so the server has no toggle race — only the test does, and it handles it by rebuilding the GraphRunner per arm. (b) m_cap sizing is untouched, so the grouped GEMMs and their padding are bit-for-bit what the accepted row measured; only step 4 moves. (c) The prefill-step arm (-259 ms) is bigger than the mixed-step arm (-162 ms) and the prediction deliberately uses the SMALLER one, because exp-0021's rejection showed the box has far fewer mixed steps than the cohort model assumes and exp-0025's delivered number matched its mixed-step figure.
